# Introduction

Homeownership is one of the largest and most significant financial commitments many people will make in their lives, and lending institutions must cautiously assess loan applications to determine whether applicants meet their lending criteria. Most applicants do not fully understand the factors influencing loan approval decisions beyond their own financial circumstances, and this analysis strives to provide insights into the home loan approval process.

The project aims to predict whether a home loan application will be approved using a machine learning classification model. In additional, the report seeks to identify the three customer segments most likely to receive loan approval. 

The [Finance Loan Approval Prediction Data](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/krishnaraj30/finance-loan-approval-prediction-data/data) dataset, available on Kaggle, is used to investigate these questions. Each observation represents a loan application with variables including the number of dependents, education level, credit history, and property area. The target variable indicates whether the loan application was approved or rejected.

We trained a Logistic Regression model to compare performance against a DummyClassifier baseline. Model performance is evaluated using accuracy, F1 score, and ROC AUC. We then examine the model’s predictions to identify three customer segments with the highest predicted likelihood of loan approval. Identifying these segments may help reveal patterns in loan approval decisions and provide insight into which applicant characteristics are associated with higher predicted approval probabilities.
